sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: L2: stable cell line shows SIGLEC12–FLAG at the plasma membrane and cytosolic puncta during necroptosis by confocal microscopy; L1: transfected cells show FLAG signal by IF; L3: FLAG detected by immunoblot. Necroptosis function (TSE-induced cell death) is preserved in the tagged line. No surface-specific (non-permeabilized) staining or flow cytometry reported to confirm extracellular FLAG accessibility.
sites.rationale: SIGLEC12 is a type I transmembrane protein with a signal peptide (residues 1–18) and a single extracellular N-terminus beginning at residue 19 (K); the C-terminus (503–595) is intracellular. Because exactly one terminus is extracellular, a terminus-placed FLAG tag must reside after the SP cleavage site (insert_after_residue = 18, residue_before = A, residue_after = K), computed from the authoritative landmarks. The insertion point is 463 residues from the TM boundary, well clear of any steric constraint. No clip names a residue, so position_evidence is topology_derived. Full-length SIGLEC12–FLAG constructs were expressed in HeLa-RIPK3–HA cells (L1), in a stable HT-29 SIGLEC12-KO line (L2), and in 293T cells (L3); all are membrane-anchored, full-length constructs detected by anti-FLAG immunofluorescence, immunoprecipitation, and immunoblot. No clip states the FLAG position in sequence, but SIGLEC12 is type I single-pass with exactly one extracellular terminus (mature N-terminus after SP cleavage at residue 18/19) and an intracellular C-terminus (503–595); the FLAG must therefore reside at the mature N-terminus.

sources.claim: SIGLEC12 was localized to the plasma membrane and cytosolic puncta during necroptosis. d , Human normal colon and colon tumour tissue biopsies from patients were stained with SIGLEC12 ( n = 3). e , The HT-29- SIGLEC12 -KO-SIGLEC12–FLAG stable cell line was treated with TSE, and SIGLEC12–FLAG was immunoprecipitated and analysed by transmission electron microscopy. f , g , HT-29 cells ( f ) and HT-29- SIGLEC12 -KO-SIGLEC12–FLAG stable cells ( g ) were treated with TSE for the indicated times.

literature_notes: All three ledger clips (L1, L2, L3) report full-length SIGLEC12–FLAG constructs but none states the FLAG position in sequence. The topology_derived rule applies because SIGLEC12 has exactly one extracellular terminus (mature N-terminus, residue 19, after SP cleavage at 18/19) and an intracellular C-terminus; a terminus-placed FLAG must therefore be at the N-terminus. L3 also describes a truncated SIGLEC12-ΔN–FLAG (residues 22–410) that lacks the TM domain (482–502) and is therefore a soluble ectodomain construct — disqualified per the rules. No clip names an internal loop insertion. Confidence is medium rather than high because no clip explicitly confirms the FLAG is N-terminal or surface-accessible (e.g., by live-cell non-permeabilized staining or flow cytometry).
